title: GBX Professional Services, 30-second brand commercial, six 5-second clips
how_to_use: Six separate clips, one per beat, each 5 seconds. Clips 1 to 5 are text to video on Seedance 2.5. Clip 6 is image to video from the designed end card (docs/gbx-endcard-1920.png), so the wordmark and closing line are pixel-exact rather than generated. On-screen text inside the AI clips has been removed on purpose: the 'Super, explained.' slide title and the 'Education, not advice.' lower third are added in the edit, which removes the spelling risk entirely. Generate at 480p to check, then 1080p for the final, and assemble in a video editor with a 0.3 second cross-fade between clips.

voice.direction: One male voiceover across all six clips: mature, in his sixties, warm and unhurried, friendly with a wry edge, the wisdom of someone who has seen a few cycles and is still curious about new technology. Measured baritone, precise diction, neutral accent with a light Australian and New Zealand lean. Sounds like a trusted mentor explaining something over a coffee, not a presenter. No sales energy, no echo, natural pauses.
voice.consistency_note: Each clip generates its own voice, so the six reads will differ slightly. For a broadcast-quality result, generate the voiceover once as a single 30-second track (an AI voice service or a session with a real voice actor using the direction above) and lay it over the clips in the edit, setting generateAudio to true only for ambience. The drafts keep the voice in each clip so you can judge the direction.
voice.avoid: Do not name a real actor or public figure in the prompt. OpenArt models do not reproduce a specific person's voice or likeness, and a request to imitate one can be refused. The description above gets the same feel.

shared_style: Cinematic brand film, editorial and premium. Dark charcoal and deep teal palette with warm off-white highlights, fine film grain, soft directional light, shallow depth of field, slow deliberate camera movement. Real-feeling Australian professionals in their thirties to fifties, diverse, natural and unposed, in a modern Melbourne office with the city skyline through glass. No stock-photo smiles, no pointing at screens, no logos, no text of any kind on screen. Minimal music: a low ambient pad with a soft piano motif, quiet room tone. Voice always clear above the music.

params.prompt: SHARED_STYLE. Dawn over the Melbourne skyline seen from a high office window, the city still quiet, first light arriving on the glass. One slow push-in toward an empty desk by the window with a closed notebook and a cup of coffee. No people, no text. VOICE_DIRECTION. VOICEOVER, spoken calmly across the whole clip: "Most businesses don't need more advice. They need a clearer picture."

SHARED_STYLE. Inside the office in soft morning light. A woman in her forties studies a calm dashboard of teal charts on a monitor, then a gentle lateral track reveals two colleagues at a whiteboard walking through a process map with a marker. Ordered, unhurried, no text legible on any screen or board. VOICE_DIRECTION. VOICEOVER: "GBX Professional Services helps firms run sharper. The numbers, the process, the pipeline."

SHARED_STYLE. Close on a hand moving a single card along a pipeline board, then a man in his fifties at a laptop nods slightly as an automated report finishes on screen, the screen a soft teal glow with no legible text. A colleague passes behind with a coffee. Calm and precise. VOICE_DIRECTION. VOICEOVER: "And AI that actually earns its keep. Practical, governed, and only where it helps."

SHARED_STYLE. A bright workplace training room. A relaxed presenter in his sixties stands at the front beside a blank teal slide with no text, twenty staff of all ages listening at tables. A young employee nods as something clicks, an older colleague writes a note. Warm, attentive, no text anywhere. VOICE_DIRECTION. VOICEOVER: "We also teach people about money. Plainly, at work, in language a whole team can follow."

SHARED_STYLE. Night. A laptop on a kitchen bench, someone tapping through a simple one-question-per-screen tool on a website in the same charcoal and teal palette, a progress bar filling, a result card appearing, the screen soft-focus with no legible text. Cut to an easy handshake across an office table in daylight. VOICE_DIRECTION. VOICEOVER: "Free tools before you ever hire us. A ten-day Diagnostic when you're ready."

clips.name: End card
clips.startFrame: docs/gbx-endcard-1920.png, uploaded to OpenArt as the start frame

params.prompt: Hold this end card exactly as it is for the full clip. The text, wordmark and layout must not change, move, or be redrawn. The only motion is a very slow, subtle drift of soft teal light across the charcoal background and a faint film grain. Minimal music resolving on a single warm swell, then silence. VOICE_DIRECTION. VOICEOVER, spoken once, unhurried: "Three leaders. One operating view. GBX Professional Services."

placeholders.SHARED_STYLE: Replace with the shared_style paragraph above.
placeholders.VOICE_DIRECTION: Replace with the voice.direction paragraph above.

edit_notes: Order the clips 1 to 6 with a 0.3 second cross-fade; total runs about 29 seconds with the fades.
Add the lower third 'Education, not advice.' over clip 4 in the site's off-white sans-serif, small, bottom left.
Optionally add 'Super, explained.' to the blank slide in clip 4 with a simple corner pin, or leave the slide blank.
Music: lay one continuous ambient track under all six clips rather than using each clip's own music, so the bed does not jump at the cuts.
Log the finished cut in docs/content-review-log.md before publishing.
